title: Data-driven HLS optimization for reconfigurable accelerators
problem: Manually selecting HLS directives for FPGA designs is challenging for programmers without hardware backgrounds. An automated, fast method is needed to make FPGA programming more accessible and enable rapid design optimization.
motivation: Automating HLS directive selection removes a significant barrier to FPGA adoption and accelerates microarchitecture customization for diverse applications.
method: The approach uses a data-driven, knowledge-based method that automatically extracts and applies optimal directive configurations to source code without QoR models or meta-heuristics. It evaluates candidate configurations across 100+ benchmark applications on Xilinx ZCU104, selects directives based on empirical performance metrics, and achieves 38ms average inference latency while maintaining design feasibility.
key_novelty: Knowledge-based data-driven HLS optimization achieving 2-3 orders of magnitude speedup over genetic algorithm-based DSE while eliminating dependency on QoR models or meta-heuristics.
contributions: Ultra-fast, knowledge-based HLS directive selection without QoR models or meta-heuristics
7.2× geometric mean speedup over designer-optimized designs and 1.35× over resource over-provisioning
Comparative evaluation against GA-based DSE and state-of-the-art methods across 100+ applications
Practical implementation on Xilinx ZCU104 with 38ms average inference latency

metrics.speedup: 7.2× vs designer-optimized, 1.35× vs over-provisioning, 2-3 orders magnitude faster than GA-based DSE
metrics.other: 38ms average inference latency, high design feasibility score

limitations: Evaluation limited to single FPGA platform (Xilinx ZCU104); generalization to other FPGA vendors and broader application domains not discussed.
